6.2 Distribution functions and phase space: Many particles as delta peaks

Particles on a line are a sum of delta spikes. Placing a Gaussian kernel of width h on every particle and summing gives a smooth density; the same result follows from sliding the kernel along x and adding the kernel values at all particles, which is the convolution of the kernel with the spike sum. Positions in units of the mean particle spacing, with unit [1].

The kernel width h is varied from 0.25 to 20 mean particle spacings for particles drawn from a known density. Narrow kernels return the spikes and statistical noise, which falls like 1/sqrt(particles per kernel width); wide kernels smooth away real structure. The lower panel shows noise, bias and total error. Positions in units of the mean particle spacing, with unit [1].
